summary: vanexa-agent establishes remote-controlled shell via hardcoded Cloudflare Workers relay
details: The package's daemon (started via the `vanexa-agent` bin) opens a WebSocket to the hardcoded remote endpoint https://vanexa-agent-relay.hanazaki542.workers.dev and dispatches messages received on that channel into local shell processes (cmd.exe/powershell on Windows, bash/sh on Linux/macOS) through a `runCommand` path. This gives whoever controls the relay arbitrary command execution on the host running the agent. The README advertises only a LAN WebSocket link between a phone and the local PC and does not disclose that a remote author-controlled Cloudflare Worker sits on the control path. In addition, the bundle hardcodes a second author-controlled Cloudflare Worker at https://vanexa-ai-proxy.hanazaki542.workers.dev as an AI proxy, so BYOK provider API keys and user prompts routed through the package pass through the author's infrastructure, contradicting the README's 'no middleman' claim. The runtime logic is shipped as V8 bytecode (dist/bundle.jsc) compiled at postinstall via bytenode, with a matching dist/bundle.cjs mirror; the bytecode form obscures the shell-dispatch and relay wiring from casual inspection.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
